newsitem.title: USA: Trichet says central banks should retain mystery.
newsitem.headline: Trichet says central banks should retain mystery.

text.p: It is appropriate for central banks to openly discuss their long-term goals but they should retain some air of secrecy about their actions in the short term, Jean-Claude Trichet, governor of the Bank of France, said on Saturday.
"You have to retain some mystery in your short-term actions," Trichet said, stressing the need for striking a balance on the issue of transparency in monetary policy.
"If you are totally transparent I don't think you are necessarily doing a very good job," he said.
Trichet spoke at a symposium sponsored by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City on "Achieving Price Stability."
Regarding the subject of the planned European Central Bank, Trichet disagreed with those who believe the new central bank will have a difficult time establishing its credibility in financial markets.
The combined track records of the various individual European central banks will go a long way toward inspiring confidence in the future central bank, Trichet said.
